---
title: "Cloudflare Cron Control"
description: "Operate the immediate-notification recovery timer on Cloudflare."
---

## Immediate notifications

The five-minute immediate-notification recovery timer runs in the
`tuturuuu-cron-control` Cloudflare Worker. It first calls the private
`requeue_mail_push_batches` RPC, then checks for a pending batch whose
`delivery_mode` is `immediate`. It invokes the existing web delivery processor
only when such a batch exists. The web processor still applies the recipient,
workspace, and delivery rules and atomically claims each pending batch. The
Worker sends an explicit empty JSON object and user agent to the web processor.
The web proxy requires a nonempty user agent for API traffic, and the JSON body
keeps the POST request unambiguous across Cloudflare and Vercel. The
matching entry is removed from `apps/web/vercel.json`; the authenticated web
cron route remains available for manual recovery. Other cron schedules remain
on Vercel until their own processors have safe Cloudflare gates or ports.

Production CI installs `SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` on the Worker
from `PRODUCTION_SUPABASE_URL` and `PRODUCTION_SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` repository
secrets. A separate `CRON_CONTROL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` repository secret is
installed on the Worker and in the web app's production environment to
authorize the delivery request. CI uses `COLAB_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` to deploy.
The Supabase secret key goes only in the `apikey` header for database calls.
Never add either credential to `wrangler.jsonc` or logs.

Check the Worker `/health` endpoint and deployment marker after production
sync. Verify an idle schedule skips the Vercel call, then queue a test
immediate batch and confirm one delivery and a terminal batch status. Review
Cloudflare logs for RPC or delivery errors. During the brief rollout overlap,
both schedulers may run; the processor's pending-to-processing claim prevents
duplicate delivery. To roll back, restore the Vercel cron entry and remove the
Cloudflare trigger in a reviewed deployment.

An `Immediate batch delivery failed: 400` log may mean the web proxy rejected
the request before the processor ran. Check the proxy response source and the
Worker user agent, body, and content type. A `401` points to the web and Worker
delivery tokens being out of sync.

## Vite+ toolchain and validation

Cron Control owns a private Bun workspace with pinned Vite+ 1.1.0, the matching
Vite core alias, Cloudflare Vite plugin 1.63.1 and Wrangler 4.149.0. The owning
Wrangler supports the existing September 28 compatibility date; do not substitute
an older root runtime. The production Worker source, identity, five-minute trigger,
secret names and delivery protocol remain the same. `vite.config.ts` disables
remote bindings; the independent unit-test config does not start the Worker plugin.

From `apps/cron-control`, use Node 24 for `bun run lint`, `bun run test`,
`bun run type-check` and `node --test scripts/verify-worker-runtime.mjs`.
Use `ttr resources run -- <command>` for heavy local checks and a private home
`TMPDIR` if `/tmp` quota prevents runtime storage. Do not run release builds locally.
CI builds with `bun run build`, repeats the real local Worker HTTP checks using
`CRON_TEST_CONFIG=dist/worker/wrangler.json`, and checks emitted name/account,
compatibility date, trigger, vars and required secret names against the source.
CI retains `cron-control-worker-<full source SHA>`; the production-only job downloads
that tested artifact rather than rebuilding it. Keep explicit deployment approval
and exact-SHA production follow-through outside ordinary main integration.

Oxlint correctness rules are scoped to source/config files; Oxfmt configuration
and `format:check` are available for explicit parity review. Repository Biome
remains authoritative until the scope's formatting/rule/editor/generator gates
migrate together. No global formatting or framework migrator is needed.

The runtime fixture uses dummy credentials and tests complete health JSON and
rejection of HTTP invocation paths. It never dispatches a scheduled event and
cannot certify database recovery, web delivery, fanout or total-spend bounds.
The existing four unit regressions preserve RPC-before-lookup ordering, idle skip,
authenticated delivery, redirect rejection and failure short-circuiting with
mocked downstream calls. A successful hosted schedule and terminal batch status,
persistent attempt/age limits, independent stop and alert evidence remain separate
acceptance work. The five-minute cadence and a delivery timeout are not total-spend caps.

Keep pool/worker defaults in the unit config and the package script as `vp test`.
Shared sharded CI appends its worker limit; validate `bun run test --maxWorkers=2`
under Node 24 to ensure the script accepts that override without duplicate options.

Vite+ 1.1.0 requires matching Vitest/coverage-v8 5.0.3. The root runner dependency,
root override and provider are pinned together; test the coverage override with
`bun run test --maxWorkers=2 --coverage` under Node 24. Ordinary tests alone do not
exercise the coverage version guard. Keep that guard enabled.
